bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruption in Strait of Hormuz affecting 80%+ import dependence for Ammonia/Sulphur; Delay in government subsidy revision for Kharif 2026; Erratic monsoon forecast (below normal predicted); Inventory valuation losses if RM prices correct sharply.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Operationally confident on volumes and integration success; Cautious/Prudent on near-term fertilizer margins due to external macro/geopolitical factors; Transparent about one-off accounting distortions.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The reported PAT collapse is almost entirely accounting-driven (land sale comp + impairment), masking strong operational cash generation; NACL's margin expansion is capped at ~9-10% until new formulation registrations mature, limiting immediate consolidated margin upside despite revenue scale.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

deepdive.thesis: Coromandel delivered record operational volumes and diversified earnings via NACL integration, but Q4 PAT was severely impacted by one-off impairments and prior-year land sale comparables. The critical near-term pivot is the mismatch between soaring global raw material costs (Ammonia/Sulphur) due to Middle East tensions and lagging government subsidy revisions, creating margin uncertainty for Q1/Q2FY27 despite strong volume growth.

risks.note: FY 2025-26 saw a sharp escalation in raw material prices, particularly in the second half, increasing cost pressures across the value chain; fertiliser inputs and energy prices firmed even as broader commodity markets stayed stable.
risks.risk: Raw material price escalation and input cost inflation

risks.note: Supply disruptions from the Middle East and China, unplanned outages and logistics bottlenecks tightened availability of ammonia, urea, sulphur and phosphates; shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea keep global supply chains under pressure and freight/energy costs elevated into FY27.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to fertiliser input supply and shipping

risks.note: Erratic distribution and delayed withdrawal of the southwest monsoon affected crop cycles and rural consumption in October-November; a transition to El Nino conditions could bring drier conditions across key agricultural regions and hit crop yields.
risks.risk: Monsoon and weather dependence, including a transition to El Nino

risks.note: Phosphate markets stayed tight amid China's export restrictions and high input costs, while potash firmed on supply constraints and geopolitical risk — a direct exposure for a phosphatics-led producer.
risks.risk: Concentrated phosphate supply and China export restrictions

risks.note: The year was impacted by a slowdown in consumption demand; Indian Agri GDP growth moderated to about 3% (from 4.2%) on uneven climatic conditions and softening food commodity prices, and global fertiliser demand growth was constrained by lower crop realisations, high interest rates and currency pressures.
risks.risk: Demand slowdown and softening agri-commodity realisations

risks.note: Sector economics rest on government policy — crop insurance, interest subvention, PM-AASHA price support, PM-KISAN income support and fertiliser policy; global markets are described as highly sensitive to policy changes and interventions.

Delays in the IMO net-zero framework and a phased, uneven rollout of carbon border adjustment mechanisms (CBAM) led to deferment or reassessment of certain low-carbon fertiliser projects, creating investment-timing uncertainty; green hydrogen/green ammonia shifts have long-term implications for the fertiliser industry.

The United States imposed reciprocal and additional tariffs on Indian exports during the year, introducing uncertainty in export markets and accelerating supply-chain diversification and regionalisation.
risks.risk: Trade protectionism and tariffs on Indian exports

sk.overview: The agrochemicals (crop protection) industry covers the development, manufacture and distribution of insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and plant growth regulators in Formulations and Technicals form. Per the issuer-commissioned ICRA Report (February 2026), the sector is supported by resilient Indian agriculture (healthy reservoir levels, robust crop production sustaining rural demand), a global 'China+1' shift favouring Indian chemical manufacturing, and sustained government fiscal support to agriculture and manufacturing.
